A.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 500 and inconsistent with $F\Delta t = \Delta p$ for a $0.5 \text{ kg}$ ball changing velocity by $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 100; it does not give an impulse of about $10 \text{ N s}$ when multiplied by $0.10 \text{ s}$.

C.explanation: This uses the difference of speeds $12 - 8 = 4 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, giving $0.5 \times 4 / 0.10 = 20 \text{ N}$, but rebound means velocities have opposite signs so changes add.

D.explanation: Total velocity change is $12 + 8 = 20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $\Delta p = 0.5 \times 20 = 10 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ and $F = 10/0.10 = 100 \text{ N}$.

hints: Notice the diagram shows $12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ toward the wall and $8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ away from it, so momentum changes direction and sign matters.
Recall impulse links force and momentum change by $F\Delta t = \Delta p = m(v - u)$ with $u$ and $v$ given opposite signs.
Take toward the wall as positive, so $u = +12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v = -8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, then find the magnitude of $m(v-u)$ before dividing by $0.10 \text{ s}$.
walkthrough: Choose a direction as positive, for example toward the wall. Then initial velocity $u = +12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and rebound velocity $v = -8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ because it is along the original path but opposite in direction.
State the impulse rule: average force $\times$ contact time equals change in momentum, $F\Delta t = \Delta p = m(v-u)$.
Substitute with units: $\Delta p = 0.5 \times (-8 - 12) = 0.5 \times (-20) = -10 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$. The magnitude of impulse is $10 \text{ N s}$.
Divide by contact time: $|F| = |\Delta p|/\Delta t = 10/0.10 = 100 \text{ N}$ away from the wall.

Using $12-8 = 4 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ would ignore the reversal and give $20 \text{ N}$, which is the common error. Adding the speeds accounts for stopping and re-launching in the opposite direction. This is option D
